title: Geometry of the deformation of a section
statement:
In the conventions of [sk-def-purity-conv] let $g:V\to B$ be smooth of pure
relative dimension $d$ with closed section $s$, and let $N_s\to B$ be the
normal bundle of $s$ with zero section $0_N$ and projection $\pi_N$. Then:

1. **(1)** *the fibres.* The fibre of $\widetilde g$ over $1$ is
$(g:V\to B,s)$ and the fibre over $0$ is $(\pi_N:N_s\to B,0_N)$; writing
$i_0,i_1:B\to\Aaf^1_B$ for the two sections, base change gives
$Li_1^{*}\mathcal F\simeq\mathcal C(g,s)$ and
$Li_0^{*}\mathcal F\simeq\mathcal C(\pi_N,0_N)$.
1. **(2)** *coordinates.* Since $s$ is a section of a smooth map, there
are étale-locally coordinates $x_1,\dots,x_d$ on $V$ over $B$ in which $s$
is $x_i=0$; on the deformation chart $u_i=x_i/t$, so $\widetilde g$ is smooth
of pure relative dimension $d$.
1. **(3)** *the punctured trivialization.* Over $\mathbf G_{m,B}$ the
deformation space is canonically $V\times_B\mathbf G_{m,B}$ with
$\widetilde s=s\times1$, so base change gives a canonical
$\kappa^{\circ}:j^{*}\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j^{*}a^{*}\mathcal C(g,s)$,
where $a:\Aaf^1_B\to B$.
1. **(4)** *the standard pair.* For $(\Aaf^d_B\to B,0)$ the deformation
space is $\Aaf^d_B\times_B\Aaf^1_B$ with $x_k=tu_k$, the family object is
$a^{*}0^{*}\omega_{\Aaf^d_B/B}$, and $0^{*}\omega_{\Aaf^d_B/B}=\Lambda(d)[2d]$
by the purity isomorphism of [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity]
($\omega_{\Aaf^d_B/B}\cong\Lambda(d)[2d]$, pulled back along the zero
section).
1. **(5)** *base change.* All of this commutes with base change in $B$
and with étale localization.

proof.text: The conventions [sk-def-purity-conv] define the normal cone from the ideal of $s$, the blow-up deformation, $\mathcal C(g,s)=Ls^*\omega_g$, and $\mathcal F=L\widetilde s^*\omega_{\widetilde g}$. Their exceptional inverse image is the constructible finite-coefficient functor of [sk-def-sf-operations](vi), on finite-type $k$-schemes. These are the finite $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ coefficient and geometric conventions of [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry]. Apply that existing same-unit theorem to $(g,s)$ with the normal bundle determined by the ideal of $s$. Its first clause identifies the geometric fibres and gives $Li_1^*\mathcal F\simeq\mathcal C(g,s)$ and $Li_0^*\mathcal F\simeq\mathcal C(\pi_N,0_N)$. Its second clause gives the relative étale coordinates $u_i=x_i/t$ and smoothness of pure dimension $d$; its third gives the canonical punctured trivialization of the pair and the family object; its fifth gives arbitrary base change, including étale localization. These are clauses (1), (2), (3), and (5) here. The theorem concerns the ideal-defined normal cone, not an arbitrary auxiliary normal-cone datum.

For the standard pair, clause (4) of [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry] gives $\mathcal D_0(\mathbf A^d_B)=\mathbf A^d_B\times_B\mathbf A^1_B$, with $x_k=tu_k$, and identifies $\mathcal F$ with $a^*(0^*\omega_{\mathbf A^d_B/B})$. Apply [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] to the trivial rank-$d$ vector bundle $\pi:\mathbf A^d_B\to B$ with zero section $0$. Its stated special case $\omega_\pi\simeq\Lambda_{\mathbf A^d_B}(d)[2d]$ pulls back to $0^*\omega_\pi\simeq\Lambda_B(d)[2d]$. Pulling this once more along $a$ gives the asserted standard family object. The purity theorem's base-change compatibility gives compatibility of this identification. Only finite coefficients $A$ are used.

Statement: the item matches main-20261015 sk-lem-geometry/_section.md clause by clause. The only change replaces the dangling [sk-prop-an] reference by [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity], which keeps the same formula and hypotheses and is the node the blueprint's lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry (4) cites. Coefficients and functors: sk-def-purity-conv with sk-def-sf-operations(vi) defines Rf^! = nu^* f^x Rnu_* on D^b_ctf(-, A_{E,n}) for separated finite-type maps of finite-type k-schemes. This is the same functor as def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image under def-pur-conventions, and the deformation space, family object and normal cone are defined the same way as in def-pur-dnc-section-family and def-pur-normal-bundle. So the hypotheses are exactly those of def-pur-section-invariant and lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry, with none missing on either side. Step 1: the statement of the same-unit lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry, clauses (1), (2), (3) and (5), gives item clauses (1), (2), (3) and (5). 'Etale localization' in (5) means etale localization on B in this chapter: prop-pur-dnc-family-constancy (4) and thm-pur-dnc-invariance say so, and the sole proof citer sk-thm-dnc does its own etale charts on V and takes only base-change identifications from (5). Etale localization on B is base change along an etale B'->B, which the cited clause (5) covers. Step 2: lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry (4) gives the standard-pair space and family object, cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity with rank r=d gives omega = Lambda(d)[2d], and pulling back along the zero section is elementary. Route: cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity is in unit sk-prop-an, which unit sk-lem-geometry cites, so it is on route and the declared tool_use is unnecessary; no tool_use needs recording.
